summary: Expanded the Slurm documentation with single-node serving, corrected multi-node serving, offline batch inference, and Apptainer/Singularity examples. The multi-node example now derives task ranks from SLURM_PROCID inside each srun task, uses current CLI flag names, bounded health checks, distinct task logs, configurable ports, and explicit cluster-specific limitations.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before evidence that the base documentation did not use task-local SLURM_PROCID ranks or Slurm per-task %n log names.

Five tests syntax-checked every embedded Bash example, guarded against outer-shell rank expansion, parsed the offline Python program and its __main__ guard, checked container rank handling and NVIDIA/ROCm guidance, and compared documented server flags with the prepared checkout's live CLI help.
Python syntax of the regression test.
Existing documentation navigation configuration remains valid JSON.
Mintlify CLI availability; it is not installed in the prepared environment, so rendered-site validation was unavailable.

gpu_execution_evidence: This is a Slurm documentation/examples feature. The prepared node is not a Slurm allocation, and no multi-node Slurm GPU cluster or qualifying model weights were available. No startup smoke or unrelated local GPU run is claimed as validation.
remaining_limitations: The examples were not submitted end to end to a real Slurm GPU cluster.
Multi-node NCCL/RCCL connectivity, site-specific scheduler directives, network-interface selection, port policy, and shared-filesystem performance remain cluster-specific and unverified here.
Apptainer/Singularity GPU passthrough was not exercised on NVIDIA or AMD hardware.
DeepSeek V3/R1 and Llama 405B weights were unavailable, so model loading, semantic accuracy, and distributed numerical output were not tested.
The Mintlify CLI was unavailable, so mint validate and rendered-site checks were not run.
No native code changed, so a native rebuild and GPU numerical reference are not applicable.
